title: [YSQL] Incorrect EXPLAIN estimates for seek/next/roundtrip counts in Bitmap Index Scan on secondary index
body:
Jira Link: [DB-17185](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-17185)
### Description

* Estimated seeks & nexts too high - the values include the seeks & nexts for fetching column values from the base table while bitmap tree nodes only return `ybctid` (rowid).
* Estimated roundtrips is always 0 with an index on colocated table - unlike `Index Scan`, the `ybctid`s are sent to PG for bitmap and/or even when it's colocated.
* The estimates are not spot on but more reasonable for PK bitmap scans.
* These incorrect values in the EXPLAIN output is *not* the direct cause of too high costs of `Bitmap Index Scan on t100000_c2  (cost=0.00..2144.91 rows=9196 width=0) (actual time=6.606..6.606 rows=9000 loops=1)` relative to its execution time since [they are computed separately](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/40dae01b20de1291f4948a24d2624f6f6c8c2daf/src/postgres/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L8396).
* Reproducible on recent master (7834a7dbca3f78d6bc7ee1cfa4a95d52398a5d8e, tag: 2.27.0.0-b203)


Example:
TAQO `cost-validation-bitmapscans`, query hash: 582465f7c9e5ccd3db1bbb8acacceffa:

Test case (from taqo model: `cost-validation-bitmapscans`)
```
drop database if exists colocateddb;
create database colocateddb with colocation = on;
\c colocateddb
drop table if exists t100000;
create table t100000 (c1 int, c2 int not null, c3 int, c4 int, c5 int, c6 int, v char(1024), primary key (c1 asc));
create unique index t100000_c2 on t100000 (c2 asc);

select setseed(0.222);
insert into t100000
  select i, i2,
         nullif((i3+4)/5, (100000+4)/5),
         nullif((i4+9)/10, (100000+9)/10),
         i5,
         nullif((i6+99)/100, (100000+99)/100),
         lpad(sha512(i5::text::bytea)||sha512(i::text::bytea)::text, 1024, '-')
    from (
      select i,
          row_number() over (order by random()) i2,
          row_number() over (order by random() + 1) i3,
          row_number() over (order by random() + 2) i4,
          row_number() over (order by random() + 3) i5,
          row_number() over (order by random() + 4) i6
        from generate_series(1, 100000) i
    ) v order by 1;

analyze t100000;

set yb_enable_cbo = on;
set yb_parallel_range_rows = 0;
set yb_enable_bitmapscan = on;
set enable_seqscan = off;

explain (analyze, dist, debug, summary off)
SELECT *
FROM   t100000
WHERE  c1 <= 9000
    or c2 <= 9000;
```
